messages.subject: Re: GSoC 2017 Adding project outline to the wiki?
messages.subject_clean: GSoC 2017 Adding project outline to the wiki?
messages.body_plain:
Google allows organizations to pick projects however they like.

R's practice has been to rank proposals first: it is usually pretty
obvious which student applications have received enough care to be viable.

Also, we require at least two mentors, who must be from different
companies or academic postings.  In all but very rare cases, one mentor
should have prior GSoC experience.  If the proposal intends to extend
some existing package or functionality, at least one of the mentors
should be a maintainer or committing author for that package.

Having a student in mind for a proposed project is fine, and often
happens for R GSoC projects, but the proposal and application must stand
on their own.

- Brian (as org. admin)

messages.body_plain:
Hi, Sakshi,

My personal suggestion is to post the outline of project.

It is easier for our administrators to know how many projects we will have in this year. I think this is important during the organization application step.

Other people can also know what has been proposed and will be done. It can also be used as a reference for students in the future.

Best,

Qiang Kou

messages.subject: Two new ideas in Biodiversity
messages.body_plain:
Dear Mentors and Students,

Just posted two new project ideas on ideas page <https://github.com/rstats-gsoc/gsoc2017/wiki/table-of-proposed-coding-projects> related to biodiversity data.

First one is Integrating biodiversity data curation functionality <https://github.com/rstats-gsoc/gsoc2017/wiki/Integrating-biodiversity-data-curation-functionality> dealing with integrating several data cleaning functions available is different packages in a single workflow.

Second one is Biodiversity data cleaning <https://github.com/rstats-gsoc/gsoc2017/wiki/Biodiversity-data-cleaning> which will deal with adding new functionality to biodiversity data cleaning pipelines.

Mentors please provide your feedback on the ideas. And students, if you are interested in the ideas, work on the tests and contact us.

Regards,

Vijay

--
---
Vijay Barve
http://vijaybarve.net/
---

Hello,
I am Krishna. A masters student in data mining currently in Barcelona. I would like to work with Professor Julien Jacques (Who is also attached in the mail) on co-clustering model for ordinal data and has agreed to be my mentor.

Scope:
a) Shiny Web Interface
b) Optimise execution time by refactoring code using  RcppAmardillo package
c) Create a user friendly R package.

I am looking for another mentor to help with this project and would appreciate guidance on how to proceed further.

Regards,
Krishna
kkalyan.in <http://kkalyan.in>

messages.subject: R has been accepted!
messages.body_plain:
I'm happy to report that Google has annouced that R has been officially accepted as a mentoring organization for GSOC2017! https://summerofcode.withgoogle.com/organizations/4947241283354624/

Thanks to all who have contributed to our wiki projects list https://github.com/rstats-gsoc/gsoc2017/wiki/table%20of%20proposed%20coding%20projects

Students, now it is time to start working on project applications. Before submitting an application, make sure to complete some project tests, and get in touch with mentors via email.
